objects.name: Red Inscription
pages:
Though sacred numbers are many,
only one may be divided into two equal parts.
In the land of that solitary number, the next words await.

objects.name: Blue Inscription
pages:
Among the sacred numbers,
only the first knows the art of dividing itself into two equal parts.
Yet none of the sacred ones that follow possess that art.

Seek the smallest among those who lack this gift.
In the land of that number, something awaits the traveler.

objects.name: Traveler
pages:
Beginnings are always special.
But if something is merely the first, others will follow in time.
What is interesting is being both the first and the only one.

...Apparently, there's a number like that.
That's all. Just a thought.

objects.name: Traveler
pages:
There isn't necessarily just one beginning.
What comes first depends on what you're counting.
...That's what the inscription over there is saying.
That's all. Just a thought...

objects.name: Traveler gazing at an island
pages:
I'm looking at that island.
...

Were you sent to this world too?
...I see. You too.

Where did you come from?
...No, sorry. You can't remember, can you?

It's the same for all of us.
None of us can remember anything from before we came here.

I tried to remember too.
Though I don't even know what I'm supposed to remember.

How many days has it been since I got here...?
I haven't been here that long, but the days are short in this place.

I'm not as used to it as the ones who have been here forever.
...I still stand here thinking about it, after all.

You never get hungry or sleepy.
At first, I thought that sounded easy enough.

But when you can just stand around doing nothing...
You find you can keep doing it forever.

...Have you explored this island yet?
If not, you should take a little walk.

There's a blue inscription and a red one, right?
Apparently, they each have their own purpose.

The blue inscriptions lead to things that help you on your journey.
The red ones lead to its end.

...Someone I met here told me that.
He has already gone on to another island.

And every island has a number.
You should remember that.

I thought they were just landmarks.
...But apparently, they are very important.

The inscriptions point to island numbers.
Understand the words, and you'll know where to go.

I've given it some thought myself.
...Only thought, though. I'm still here.

I do want to go home.
Even though I can't remember anywhere to go home to.

Is someone waiting for me out there?
...If I've kept them waiting, I feel bad about that.

But if someone told me I could go home right now...
Would I be able to say yes straight away?

If I stay here, I don't have to remember anything.
...Sometimes I catch myself thinking that.

You're going on, aren't you?
Then go while your legs still want to move.

I'll keep looking a little longer.
...I wonder if there's someone on that island too.

objects.name: Person sitting on the rooftop
pages:
Jumping off there won't kill you.
...I wonder why. It just hurts.

Jumping into the sea is no use either.
A fish eats you...and again, it just hurts.

That fish doesn't like people diving into its home.
It leaves you alone if you swim on the surface.

If you know that, you can spare yourself the pain.
...That's all, really.

...
It's nice and quiet here.

You mean to keep going, don't you?
...Have you solved the inscriptions?

noPages: ...Oh, I see. Solving riddles is fun, isn't it?

You look like someone who would rather not be told the answer. Would you like to keep thinking...?
...Or would you like me to tell you?

yesPages:
Then I'll tell you.
Just the answers.

Red is 2. Blue is 3.
...Those are the numbers the inscriptions point to.

2 is next door.
3 is very close too.

See the fellow standing on that platform?
It's the island he is always looking at.

...You don't have to thank me.
You asked, so I answered.

objects.name: Huddled figure
pages:
I was collecting stones,
lining them up to pass the time.
But no matter how hard I tried, I couldn't arrange them in a rectangle.

Then someone told me,
'That's something very sacred.'

But I went and found more stones,
and this time I made a neat rectangle.

Then he looked sad and said,
'It isn't sacred anymore. It won't receive any blessings now.'

He said it was
something very important.

objects.name: Red Inscription
pages:
In the beginning, there was one who made heaven and earth.
He parted light from darkness,

set the sea apart from the land,
and filled the earth with every living thing.

At last, his work of creation was complete,
and he made the following day a sacred day of rest.

Count the days from the beginning of creation.
In the land of that number, the next words await.

objects.name: Traveler
pages:
I read a novel once.
What was the title...? Something about everything turning into a certain letter of the alphabet, I think.

There was a story about a lonely number in it.
...Yes, reading that inscription just reminded me.
That's all. Just a thought...

objects.name: Blue Inscription
pages:
Among the sacred numbers are those whose reflections, too, hold sacred power.
Find the two smallest pairs.

In the four lands facing one another across the mirror,
things that aid the traveler are said to sleep.

objects.name: Traveler
pages:
Numbers in a mirror...
Apparently, some numbers keep the same property when you read their digits backward.

And they become a different number from the original.
...Perhaps this inscription wants us to find the smaller pairs among them.
Well, I don't really understand it myself.
...Sacred, hm.
'Dercas.'
I was just reading it backward...

objects.name: Huddled figure
pages:
Whenever an inscription calls something 'sacred,' it means the same thing.
They were all written by the same person, after all.
Well, people had all sorts of names for it long ago.

The blue inscription isn't here.
Try somewhere with a little more fresh air.

objects.name: Potion of Speed
pages: You drank the potion. Your sprint speed increased.

objects.name: Potion of Leaping
pages: You drank the potion. Your jump strength increased.

objects.name: Potion of Leaping
pages: You drank the potion. Your jump strength increased.

objects.name: Potion of Speed
pages: You drank the potion. Your sprint speed increased.

objects.name: Blue Inscription
pages:
Once there lived a sage who knew the depths of number.
He laid anew the foundations of geometry.

In the year formed by twice nine hundred and eighty-three,
a great honor was bestowed upon his wisdom, yet he did not appear at the ceremony.
Yet no sage is beyond error.
There was a number he called sacred and indivisible.
That number was neither sacred nor indivisible.
Seek the land of the number the sage mistook.

objects.name: Traveler
pages: You would think a great sage knows everything, wouldn't you?
But even the finest mind can be mistaken.

Sometimes it's precisely because someone is so great
that a small mistake is remembered for generations.

...Come to think of it, that inscription told of a sage like that.
That's all. Just a thought.

objects.name: Potion of Flight
pages:
You drank the potion. You gained the ability to fly.
Press F while jumping to fly continuously in the direction you are looking. Hold Shift to accelerate.

objects.name: Traveler
pages: You did well to find this place.

I mean, it isn't fair. This one isn't red.
Its number is black.

...Don't worry. It won't happen again.
Oh, what am I even saying...?

objects.name: Red Inscription
pages:
Each night, twins are born.
Seek the elder twin made sacred beneath the moon of the sixteenth night.
The next words sleep in that land.

objects.name: Traveler
pages:
It seems strange to call one twin the elder brother and the other the younger.
They are almost the same.
But look closely, and there's a small difference. One...no, two.
Well, I suppose the one born first is the elder.

Come to think of it, how many pairs of twins are there?
More than anyone could ever count, perhaps.

objects.name: Traveler
pages:
To define the natural numbers, you pick the first one, then define 'the next number.'
After 1 comes 2, after 2 comes 3, after 3 comes 4...like that.

So if you follow the definition, the smaller numbers appear first.
If numbers have brothers, I suppose the smaller one would be the elder.

objects.name: Red Inscription
pages:
Once there lived a man who sat in judgment of the law
and set hard questions before the sages.

Even centuries later, he confounded those who followed.
In a certain sequence of numbers, he discerned an unchanging law.

Yet a great sage of a later age broke it, declaring:
'No, one of these can be split in two.'
Of those two sacred fragments, seek the smaller.

objects.name: Traveler
pages:
It worked for the first five, right?
The fellow who spotted the pattern was impressive, but so was the one who disproved it.

objects.name: Traveler
pages:
Apparently, that great sage also tackled a problem about crossing seven bridges exactly once each.
And proved that you couldn't do it, no matter how you tried.
...Amazing that you can even know something like that.

objects.name: Red Inscription
pages: Fortunate is the one surrounded by companions.

Many have companions at all four corners.
Seek the fourth sacred one among them.

objects.name: Traveler
pages:
Have you found the wonderful items on those four islands yet?
You see, their numbers are very similar to the number of the island you need to find next.
Perhaps that isn't much of a hint...

...What? A map?
Are you looking for a map?

yesPages:
There are no maps in this world.
We cannot look at a map.
noPages:
It even looks very much like one of those four islands.
You'll know when you get there. ...Or perhaps not.

objects.name: Traveler
pages:
Down on the ground, you can't tell;
up in the sky, you might see well?

I climbed a tower to look around,
but the fog was too thick to see a thing.

Those slanting bridges, loved by all;
if only we had a map at all!

objects.name: Traveler
pages: Each of the four companions always has a twin.
...Well, you can tell that if you look closely at the map.

objects.name: Traveler
pages:
I've checked a hundred and thirty candidate pairs of twins, one after another, and still can't find the fourth...
The first three were easy enough.
Damn it. How many more pairs do I have to check...?

objects.name: Person gazing into the distance
pages: I know a few places where five sacred ones form a cross.
Though on the map, that cross is tilted forty-five degrees.
An island with eight bridges. The fourth of those...
...Even I can't see it from here.

objects.name: Red Inscription
pages:
The greatest sage in all of history
found a wondrous law amid lawless chaos.

Forty trials succeeded, every one.
Yet the forty-first failed, and the law was broken.
Seek the place brought forth by the final success.

objects.name: Traveler
pages:
Such a beautiful rule, but it doesn't look very beautiful on the map...
If only the first island had been 41.

objects.name: Red Inscription
pages:
There were two stonemasons.
Each carved a die of stone with his own hands, and they vied to make the larger.

The contest was always close;
the larger die was but one measure greater along each edge.
The loser cut from the winner's die a volume equal to his own.

Thus their contest was repeated many times.
On rare occasions, the stone left behind held sacred power.
The people set the sacred stones in order, from smallest to largest.

Seek the twenty-third stone.
There, the way shall open.

objects.name: Traveler
pages: What is sacred power, anyway?

I've heard that no matter how hard you strike a sacred stone, it won't split.
I suppose that's what makes it sacred.

objects.name: Traveler
pages:
A die has six identical square faces, so each number from one to six has an equal chance of coming up.
A clever shape, isn't it?

objects.name: Traveler
pages:
I was sure it meant that island country out in the tropical sea.
You know, as if some famous mathematician from there had discovered them...

...Apparently, it has nothing to do with the place.
What a confusing name...

objects.name: Traveler
pages:
Start at seven. Then add twelve, eighteen, twenty-four...in order...
Thirty-eight tries, and only now the twenty-first hit...

...Almost there.
Come on. Keep going...

objects.name: Person gazing into the distance
pages: ...It means the first kind, doesn't it?

It says 'one measure greater,' right?
Not two.
And it doesn't say to split it in half, either.

...Someone went off convinced it meant the second kind.
It's such a long way, too.
I bet he is sitting on an empty island with his head in his hands by now.

objects.name: Red Inscription
pages:
Once there lived a sage who discerned a law of odd and even.
He declared that the odd would never be outnumbered by the even.

Through tens of millions of numbers, the law held firm,
and was believed to be an eternal truth.

Decades passed, and another sage proved the law false,
though he knew not a single number at which it failed.

In time, one such failure was found,
but whether it was the smallest remained unknown.
After many more years, the smallest failure at last revealed itself.

That number is only half sacred.
It is the product of two truly sacred numbers.
Seek the greater of the two.

objects.name: Traveler
pages:
Sacred numbers...
So there are half-sacred numbers too.
But then they are no longer sacred numbers, are they...?

objects.name: Traveler
pages:
Both those numbers have five digits, so I hear.
I kept picking random five-digit numbers and trying them, but got nowhere.

Then someone else started checking them from the beginning, one by one.
He went on ahead without any trouble.
It was almost a bit of a letdown...

objects.name: Traveler
pages:
There were some digits written on the floor.
They have weathered away now. Even then, I couldn't make out some of them...
I think it was...

objects.name: Purple Inscription
pages: Once there lived a servant of God who sought the truth of numbers.

With eleven knights in his train,
he proclaimed them a sacred order to the world.

Yet two traitors lurked within their ranks,
and three true knights had not been invited.
Centuries passed, and a sage arose.

He struck down one of the false knights.
That great deed was accomplished in silence alone.

The knights who bear that servant of God's name
shall here be called the Knights of Prayer.

objects.name: Purple Inscription
pages:
In distant India, counting beats,
a poet-sage discerned a rule.

Across the sea, far to the west,
the art of reckoning came to flower.

The sequence bears a sage's name.
How many pairs will next year bring?

Those that hold sacred power
we name the Knights of Succession.

objects.name: Red Inscription
pages: Here gather the knights who pass through the Million Gate.

From the Knights of Prayer, choose the two greatest.
From the Knights of Succession, choose the single greatest.
Join the power of the three as one.

That power shall be sacred once again,
and lead thee to the end of thy long journey.

objects.name: Traveler
pages:
Goes without saying, but you can't fit through a gate if you're wider than the opening.
Apparently, even exactly a million won't fit through the 'Million Gate.'

Still, getting thrown out for being too big the moment you reach a million...
Being a knight is no easy life.

objects.name: Traveler
pages:
They say sacred numbers always lose their sacred power when you multiply them together.
But if you add them, sometimes the sacred power remains.
...The gods' favor is a fickle thing.

objects.name: Traveler?
pages:
Hello. You took your time.
I was getting tired of waiting.

...Oh?
You still haven't remembered anything?

And yet you made it all the way here.
Ha! Impressive. Just what I would expect of you.
It was your colleague who prepared this back door.

Still, what a troublesome, convoluted mechanism he made.
...Well, I can think of a reason.

You were always showing him up with your mathematics, weren't you?
I suppose this is his own little revenge. Ha ha ha.
Now then...what shall I do?

Yes, I think I'll wait here a little longer.
Perhaps another of our friends will arrive soon.
...Hm? Where is the exit?

Right there.
Go on, look up.

objects.name: Seated figure
pages: The first kind, not the second kind?
You could have written that properly...

objects.name: Stone of Escape
pages:
The stone is shining.
Will you touch it?
